The UK's 15 Best Motorcycle Roads — Ranked

We ranked the UK's finest motorcycle roads by four criteria: scenery, bends & technical challenge, surface quality, and overall rider rating. From the legendary Bealach na Ba in Scotland's remote northwest to the flowing Buttertubs Pass in Yorkshire, these are the roads every British biker should have on their bucket list.

The Rankings

  1. Bealach na Ba — Applecross, Scotland. 2,053ft climb with Alpine-grade hairpins and jaw-dropping views over Skye.
  2. Cat & Fiddle (A537) — Peak District, England. Fast, flowing, and one of the most popular biker roads in the country.
  3. Hardknott Pass — Lake District, England. 30% gradients and tight switchbacks — England's toughest road.
  4. Snake Pass (A57) — Peak District, England. Sweeping moorland curves between Manchester and Sheffield.
  5. Black Mountain Pass — Brecon Beacons, Wales. Arguably Wales' finest riding road with dramatic scenery.
  6. A686 Hartside — Pennines, England. A long, satisfying climb to one of England's highest cafés.
  7. Evo Triangle — North Wales. Three roads forming a perfect triangle of fast, technical riding.
  8. A82 Glencoe — Highlands, Scotland. Dramatic mountain scenery through Scotland's most famous valley.
  9. Kirkstone Pass (A592) — Lake District, England. The classic Lakes pass with stunning Ullswater views.
  10. Horseshoe Pass — North Wales. A sweeping mountain road above Llangollen.
  11. Honister Pass (B5289) — Lake District, England. Tight, technical, and raw mountain riding.
  12. A939 Lecht Road — Cairngorms, Scotland. High mountain pass through ski country.
  13. Cheddar Gorge — Somerset, England. Dramatic limestone cliffs and tight curves.
  14. Devil's Staircase (A896) — Highlands, Scotland. Remote single-track with serious elevation.
  15. Buttertubs Pass — Yorkshire Dales, England. Flowing moorland road between Swaledale and Wensleydale.

Explore all 48 rated roads on our UK Biker Road Ratings tool, or plan your own tour with our route builder. Read our The Ultimate Motorcycle Touring Packing List guide for more. Read our Wales: 5 Must-Ride Motorcycle Roads guide for more.
keyTakeaways: Bealach na Ba in Applecross tops the ranking, climbing 2,053ft with Alpine-grade hairpins.
England's toughest entry is Hardknott Pass, with 30% gradients and tight switchbacks.
The Peak District supplies two crowd favourites in the Cat & Fiddle (A537) and Snake Pass (A57).
Wales is best represented by the Black Mountain Pass in the Brecon Beacons.

faq.q: What is the best motorcycle road in the UK?
faq.a: Bealach na Ba near Applecross in the Scottish Highlands is our top-ranked road. Its 2,053ft climb features Alpine-grade hairpins, dramatic drop-offs and views towards Skye. It is single-track in places, so ride within your limits and use the passing places. Reward yourself at the Applecross Inn once you reach the bottom.

Each road is scored on four criteria: scenery, bends and technical challenge, surface quality and overall rider rating. Combining those factors gives a balanced picture rather than favouring pure speed or pure views. The full data set covers 48 rated roads on our UK Biker Road Ratings tool.

faq.q: Which is the hardest road on the list?
faq.a: Hardknott Pass in the Lake District is the most demanding. Gradients reach 30%, the switchbacks are tight and the road is narrow single-track with steep drop-offs. Ride it early to avoid tourist traffic, drop into first gear on the descents and let engine braking do the work.

faq.q: Are these roads suitable for beginners?
faq.a: The flowing routes like Snake Pass and the Cat & Fiddle suit newer riders, while the steep passes such as Hardknott, Honister and the Bealach demand more experience. Build confidence on the easier A-roads first, then progress to the tight mountain passes once your slow-control and hill starts are solid.

faq.q: When is the best time to ride them?
faq.a: Late spring through early autumn offers the most reliable conditions. Many of these roads sit at altitude, so they collect ice, standing water and grit in winter. Ride midweek or early morning in summer to dodge tourist traffic, and always check the forecast for the specific pass.
